questions.q: In the Markowitz mean-variance optimization problem, what is being minimized?
options: The portfolio's expected return
The portfolio's variance, w' * Sigma * w, subject to hitting a target return and weights summing to one
The number of assets in the portfolio
The correlation between any two assets
questions.explain: Markowitz's problem minimizes portfolio variance (w'Sigma*w) subject to the constraints that weights sum to one and the portfolio achieves a specified target expected return.

questions.q: What does the efficient frontier represent?
options: The single portfolio with the highest possible return regardless of risk
The set of portfolios offering the lowest possible risk for each level of expected return (or equivalently, the highest return for each level of risk)
A list of every asset available in the market
The portfolio with exactly zero risk
questions.explain: The efficient frontier is traced by solving the minimum-variance problem at every possible target return. Any portfolio below or inside the frontier is dominated by a frontier portfolio.

questions.q: What makes a portfolio 'dominated' in the mean-variance framework?
options: It has the lowest fees of any available portfolio
Another portfolio exists with the same expected return but lower risk, or the same risk but higher expected return
It contains more than ten assets
It was created before the efficient frontier was calculated
questions.explain: A dominated portfolio is strictly worse in the mean-variance sense — a rational investor would always prefer the dominating alternative, so dominated portfolios never lie on the efficient frontier.

questions.q: Which point on the efficient frontier requires no choice of target return at all?
options: The maximum-return portfolio
The market portfolio
The minimum-variance portfolio, the single portfolio with the lowest possible variance overall
Any portfolio with a Sharpe ratio of exactly 1.0
questions.explain: The minimum-variance portfolio sits at the leftmost point of the efficient frontier and is found by minimizing variance subject only to the weights summing to one — no return target constraint is needed.

questions.q: Why is the pure Markowitz framework criticized in practice, even though the math is exact?
options: Because it requires too much computing power for even a handful of assets

Because it depends on accurately estimated expected returns and a full covariance matrix, and small estimation errors — especially in expected returns — can swing the resulting 'optimal' weights dramatically
Because it cannot be applied to stocks, only to bonds
Because the formula has never been empirically tested
questions.explain: Mean-variance optimization is only as good as its inputs. Estimating expected returns and a full N x N covariance matrix accurately is difficult in practice, and the optimizer is highly sensitive to those estimation errors — a widely cited practical limitation of the pure Markowitz approach.
